articles.title: Massive landslide, not earthquake, triggered deadly Lhende disaster, scientists say
articles.summary: An international team of scientists has determined that the catastrophic flood and debris flow in Nepal's Lhende Khola region, near the border with Tibet, was caused by a massive landslide rather than an earthquake. The disaster, which struck the area on September 10, has resulted in over 1,300 confirmed deaths and many more missing persons. Seismic data analysis disproved initial earthquake assumptions, highlighting the landslide as the primary trigger. The findings underscore the need for improved landslide monitoring and disaster preparedness in the Himalayan region.

articles.title: Human rights activists and lawyers demand Home Minister apologise over threatening remarks against journalists
articles.summary: Human rights activists, senior lawyers and civic campaigners in Kathmandu have condemned Home Minister Sudhan Gurung's recent remarks, describing them as threatening toward journalists. They demanded that the minister withdraw the statements and issue a public apology. Former National Human Rights Commission member Sushil Pyakurel and senior advocate Dinesh Tripathi were among those leading the protest, urging the government to respect press freedom and uphold human rights standards.

articles.title: Heavy rain likely in some parts of these 4 provinces today
articles.summary: The Meteorological Department forecasts generally cloudy skies across Nepal on September 10, with heavy rain possible in specific hilly areas of Koshi, Bagmati, Gandaki, and Lumbini provinces, as well as in Madhesh Province and the Tarai belts of Bagmati, Gandaki, and Lumbini. Residents in these regions are advised to stay alert for sudden downpours.

articles.title: Tribhuvan Highway blocked after landslide at Sopyangkhola
articles.summary: A landslide struck Sopyangkhola in Thakre Rural Municipality-7, Dhading, around 9 pm on September 9, blocking the Tribhuvan Highway in both directions. The highway, a key link between Kathmandu and Hetauda, was halted due to continuous heavy rainfall that hampered clearance efforts. Police in Dhading reported the obstruction and warned of difficulties in restoring traffic. The incident underscores ongoing challenges with monsoon-related landslides affecting Nepal’s transport corridors.

articles.title: Rasuwa flood shows why Nepal must rethink development in hazard-prone areas
articles.summary: The recent flood in Rasuwa district underscores Nepal’s vulnerability to natural hazards and calls for a fundamental reassessment of development practices in high‑risk zones. The article explains that the young, tectonically active Himalayas, driven by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates, create ongoing seismic activity, uplift, and terrain changes that amplify flood and landslide risks. It argues that current development projects often ignore these geophysical realities, leading to repeated disasters. The piece urges policymakers to integrate hazard mapping, stricter land‑use regulations, and climate‑resilient planning into future infrastructure and settlement strategies to protect lives and reduce economic losses.

articles.title: Govt surveys flood-hit families to determine need for temporary housing
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has started surveying families displaced by the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli floods to assess the need for temporary housing. Thousands of flood victims are currently staying in emergency holding centres across the affected districts. Deputy Director General Prakash Aryal noted that not all residents in these centres may require separate temporary shelters, prompting the survey to allocate resources efficiently.

articles.title: The Project Beyond performs in Australia for Nepal flood relief
articles.summary: The Nepali music collective The Project Beyond performed at the Monsoon Mela event in New South Wales, Australia on September 6, dedicating the show to flood‑relief efforts in Nepal. The concert, held at FunHaus Factory, aimed to raise awareness and support for communities devastated by recent floods in Nepal, showcasing solidarity from the diaspora and the international music community.

articles.title: A hand pump in every yard, but no water anywhere in Betauna
articles.summary: In Betauna, a ward of Golbazar Municipality in Siraha district, residents like 45‑year‑old Chandardevi Mukhiya have hand pumps in their yards that have been dry for years. With her own pump non‑functional, she now relies on a neighbor’s submersible pump. The situation highlights a broader water scarcity problem in the community, where installed hand pumps fail to deliver water, forcing locals to depend on limited alternative sources.

articles.title: NVL’s final three league matches today; here’s what each team needs
articles.summary: The Nepal Volleyball League (NVL) reaches the climax as the final three league-stage matches are played today in Kathmandu. These games will determine which team tops the standings and secures a direct berth in the championship final, while the remaining teams will have to navigate the playoff round for a chance to reach the final. All six participating teams are competing for the crucial points that will shape the postseason.

articles.title: Who brought the controversial religious leaders to the Gen Z memorial gathering?
articles.summary: A memorial ceremony for Gen Z Martyrs' Day was held on Tuesday at the old Parliament Building premises in New Baneshwor. The event attracted criticism after organizers gave prominent stage time to two controversial religious figures, Bijay Bhandari, accused of running fraud schemes for 15 years, and Shrinivas Acharya, also known for extremist views. Observers questioned why these 'dharmagurus' were invited as guests of honour, suggesting the move politicised the gathering and undermined its solemn purpose.

articles.title: Rasuwa flood survivors face hidden health risks even after rescue
articles.summary: Following the devastating flood in Rasuwa district, survivors arriving at Kathmandu's National Trauma Centre are confronting hidden health hazards beyond obvious injuries. While some patients appear stable, doctors like Dr. Saroj Kumar Gohiwar report cases of severe internal conditions, infections, and potential long‑term ailments that were not initially evident. The article highlights the need for comprehensive medical screening, mental health support, and continued monitoring to prevent complications after rescue operations. It underscores the challenges faced by health authorities in addressing both immediate trauma and the lingering health risks that flood survivors may endure.

articles.title: Nepal seeks $20 million from loss and damage fund over Rasuwa floods
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has requested over Rs 3 billion (about $20 million) from the UN's Loss and Damage Fund, claiming that the catastrophic floods in Rasuwa district were exacerbated by climate change. A formal letter was sent to the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, seeking compensation for the disaster’s impacts.

articles.title: Deuba announces nationwide tour to reconnect with party members
articles.summary: Former Nepali Congress president Sher Bahadur Deuba announced plans for a nationwide tour to meet party members and strengthen ties. Speaking at an event organized by Nepali Congress Bhaktapur on the occasion of BP Koirala's 133rd birth anniversary, Deuba said the tour will cover various regions of Nepal, aiming to reconnect with grassroots supporters and discuss the party's future direction.

articles.title: Special Court releases German passport printer Veridos on regular date
articles.summary: The Special Court in Kathmandu ordered that Veridos, the German company responsible for printing Nepalese passports, be released on a regular date without the requirement to post bail. The bench, consisting of Special Court members Narayan Paudel and Dilli Ratna Shrestha, issued the decision, allowing Veridos to resume its activities pending further proceedings.

articles.title: Cultural discrimination in the Gurkha regiments: From recruitment to a crisis of cultural identity
articles.summary: The article examines the historical and ongoing cultural discrimination faced by Gurkha soldiers within British regiments. Beginning with recruitment after the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, the British favored certain Nepali ethnic groups such as the Gurungs and Magars, marginalizing others. Over time, these practices have contributed to a crisis of cultural identity among Gurkha veterans, who feel their traditions and community bonds are eroded by institutional biases. The piece highlights personal testimonies, policy gaps, and calls for greater recognition of the diverse Nepali communities that serve in the Gurkha regiments.

articles.title: SC dismisses writ against Former Chief Justice Rana, clears way for pension
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of Nepal has dismissed a writ petition filed against former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana, clearing the path for him to receive pension benefits and other facilities. Rana, who retired while under suspension following an impeachment motion, had previously been denied these entitlements. The court's ruling removes the legal barrier, allowing the former chief justice to access his pension.

articles.title: Parliamentary committee questions surge in sugar prices to Rs 130 per kg
articles.summary: Parliamentary committee chair Rahbar Ansari raised concerns over a sharp rise in sugar prices in Nepal, which have reached Rs 130 per kilogram. The surge is linked to India's recent ban on sugar exports, leading to higher market prices and affecting consumers. Ansari highlighted the issue during a committee meeting, emphasizing the need to protect consumer interests and address the supply shortage.

articles.title: Nepal should go to the UN to demand fairness, not sympathy
articles.summary: The August 26 flood in Nepal's Bhotekoshi‑Trishuli river system caused massive loss of life, displaced thousands, and destroyed settlements, roads, bridges and hydropower projects. The article argues that Nepal should appeal to the United Nations not for sympathy but to demand climate‑justice and equitable support, highlighting the link between the disaster and climate change. It calls for international fairness in addressing the impacts of climate‑driven events on vulnerable nations.

articles.title: Panchadan festival celebrated in Bhaktapur
articles.summary: The Panchadan festival was observed in Bhaktapur on September 9, featuring a procession of five Dipankara Buddha idols around the historic city. Celebrated annually on Bhadra Krishna Trayodashi, locally known as Panchadan Chare, the event follows Buddhist tradition. Historical records credit Jayadev Bajracharya with initiating the festival. The celebration highlights Bhaktapur's cultural heritage and religious practices.

articles.title: Truck with 1,240 kg of marijuana found in Dhankuta, driver absconding
articles.summary: Police in Dhankura, eastern Nepal, intercepted a truck on the Koshi Highway carrying approximately 1,240 kg of illegal marijuana. The massive haul was seized during a checkpoint operation, and the driver fled the scene. Hemant Bhandari Chhetri, information officer of the District Police Office, confirmed the seizure and noted that investigations are underway to locate the driver and uncover the source of the drugs.

articles.title: Nepal grapples with limited DNA analysis capacity
articles.summary: The article highlights Nepal's struggle to identify flood victims due to a severely limited DNA analysis capacity. With only about 20% of bodies recovered from recent monsoon floods, families await identification, but the country's forensic laboratories lack the equipment, trained personnel, and funding needed for large‑scale DNA profiling. Government officials, including the Prime Minister and the Minister of Home Affairs, acknowledge the shortfall and have appealed for international assistance and increased budget allocations. NGOs and the Nepal Red Cross are also stepping in, but the bottleneck threatens timely closure for grieving families and hampers disaster response efforts.

articles.title: Nepal’s youth revolt, a year later
articles.summary: A year after the September Storm protests in Kathmandu, Nepal's youth reflect on the deadly rally that sparked a nationwide movement. The article revisits the events of the September 2023 storm, examines the loss of lives, and assesses the political and social changes that have followed. Interviews with student activists reveal lingering frustrations, hopes for reforms, and the evolving role of young people in Nepal's democratic discourse.

articles.title: Gripping drama of the transgender community
articles.summary: The Nepali film "Elephants in the Fog," which highlights the struggles and resilience of the transgender community, has garnered international acclaim after winning awards at the Cannes Film Festival. The movie was recently screened in Kathmandu, drawing large audiences and sparking conversations about LGBTQ+ rights and representation in Nepalese cinema. Critics praised its poignant storytelling, strong performances, and the director’s bold approach to a marginalized subject. The screening is seen as a milestone for both the country's film industry and the visibility of transgender narratives, encouraging broader societal acceptance and inspiring local filmmakers to explore diverse stories.

articles.title: Nepal tells tourists: ‘Your Visit Matters’
articles.summary: The Nepalese government is urging tourists to visit the country, stressing that tourism revenue is a vital source of funds for rebuilding after recent disasters. Officials say that each visitor’s spending helps reconstruct infrastructure, support livelihoods, and revive local economies. The campaign highlights Nepal’s natural beauty and cultural heritage, positioning the nation as a safe and rewarding destination for international travelers.

articles.title: Preserving the diversity  of intangible heritage
articles.summary: The article discusses Nepal’s newly drafted Heritage Bill, emphasizing the need for an inclusive board to oversee the preservation of the country’s intangible cultural heritage. While the bill outlines statutory measures, critics argue that without diverse representation from communities, scholars, and practitioners, the legislation may fall short of protecting living traditions, languages, and rituals. The piece calls for broader stakeholder involvement to ensure the bill translates into effective, community‑driven preservation efforts.
